thread.title: Tim Cook doesn’t seem to know how much an iPhone costs

author: Emily Bary
title: Tim Cook doesn’t seem to know how much an iPhone costs
text:
Apple Inc. Chief Executive Tim Cook defended the price of the company’s iPhones during a Tuesday appearance on Good Morning America , saying that while the sticker prices may look expensive, a good chunk of consumers pay a more reasonable amount due to carrier subsidies.
“Even the phone that’s priced over $1,000, most people pay about $30 a month for it, so it’s about $1 a day.” Apple CEO Tim Cook on Good Morning America According to Cook , “most” iPhone owners pay about $30 a month for their devices as part of a wireless plan, even if the phone retails for upward of $1,000 outright. But judging from Apple’s AAPL, +0.50% website, that math doesn’t check out.
Apple’s own upgrade program promises an iPhone XS starting at $49.91 a month and an iPhone XS Max starting at $54.08 a month. The most expensive iPhone XS Max, which has 512 GB of storage and retails for $1,449, will set you back $68.66 a month as part of Apple’s program.
Apple didn’t immediately respond to a MarketWatch request for comment or clarification.
Don’t miss: Why would anybody buy the iPhone XS?
The Apple iPhone Upgrade Program is a 24-month plan that lets users upgrade to a new iPhone annually and includes AppleCare insurance. Apple’s “iPhone Payments” plan will get you a 512 GB iPhone XS Max for $60.37 a month, though that price doesn’t include an annual upgrade or AppleCare. AT&T Inc.’s See Also Three Senators Key to the Kavanaugh Confirmation × T, +0.49% installment program, meanwhile, gives you a 12-month or 24-month upgrade with an “eligible trade in” but no AppleCare, for a price of $60.38. Verizon VZ, -0.47% has a similarly priced option.
Even Apple’s LCD iPhone XR, which begins at $749 if you buy it outright, goes for a starting price of $37.11 a month if purchased through Apple’s upgrade program. If you want to pay just $30 or less a month for a phone through Apple’s program, you can find phones in the iPhone 8 and iPhone 7 families that qualify. The cheapest iPhone 8 Plus, for example, costs $29.12 a month through Apple’s program, but that phone only goes for $699 if you buy it upfront.
See: iPhone XR creates some drama for Apple’s new lineup
“We want to make an iPhone for everyone,” Cook said on Good Morning America . He argued that the phone remains a good value for consumers given that it’s replaced the traditional cameras and video cameras that they would’ve otherwise used.
Apple shares were up 0.7% Tuesday, but have gained 30% in 2018, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, +0.84% has gained 6% and the S&P 500 SPX, +0.67% has gained 9%.
